outcome: Core Experiment Authoring editors now use an explicit editor-language contract that is independent of stored artifact format versions
owner_impact: Configuration, Initialization, Controller and Metrics now share the same metadata-driven editor path and all four core code artifacts explicitly declare Python as their editor language. Older experiments may keep historical format identifiers such as vlab.config/0.2, vlab.initializer-state/0.2 and python-vlab/0.1 without causing the editor to fall back to plain text after hydration. Search remains unchanged.

technical_evidence: Live Supabase inspection showed retained experiments/revisions use multiple historical format identifiers for Configuration, Initialization and Controller, while Metrics consistently uses python-vlab-metrics/0.1.
The previous editor inferred Python directly from format strings and therefore classified vlab.config/0.2, vlab.initializer-state/0.2 and python-vlab/0.1 as plain text.
All four core artifacts now declare language=python through one shared artifact metadata contract; artifact serialization/runtime format remains a separate field.

The legacy three-special-editors-plus-Metrics-generic split was removed from the artifact presentation adapter: all four core textareas expose the same artifact metadata shape and use the same lookup path.

Production browser smoke explicitly rewrites the three core format fields to the historical live values after editor mount, forces authoring resynchronization, switches all four artifacts twice, and requires Python mode plus visibly distinct rendered token colors to survive.
